content: Acriflavine is a topical antiseptic agent that is available in the form of an orange or brown powder. It can cause harm if it comes into contact with the eyes or if it is inhaled. As a dye, it has the potential to stain the skin and may cause irritation upon contact. Commercially available acriflavine preparations are often combined with proflavine. This compound is known by various names in different contexts. Acriflavine was first developed in 1912 by Paul Ehrlich, a prominent German medical researcher. It was utilized during the First World War as a treatment for sleeping sickness. Chemically, it is derived from acridine. The hydrochloride form of acriflavine is known to be more irritating compared to its base form. In addition to its antiseptic properties, acriflavine is also employed in the treatment of external fungal infections in aquarium fish.
